ArtifactEnrichmentDocRequest.description:
Extract security references from an artifact and enrich them into one graded report.

Paste ``text`` and/or upload ``files`` (nmap XML, Tenable/Qualys CSV, PDF advisory, EML).
Every CVE, product, weakness, technique, and indicator found is enriched into a single
report: an SSVC decision and PATCH/BLOCK/WATCH/INFO action per reference, weaponization
scores, a prioritized worklist with KEV deadlines, ATT&CK technique mappings with detection
and mitigation guidance, kill-chain attack paths, and machine-readable exports.

attached_artifact_ids.description: LEGACY whole-run provenance: the ids of the stored artifacts whose content is in the legacy scalar `text`. Recorded on the report's `attachment_sources`, and every reference extracted from `text` carries all of them (with several, the text is a merge and only the caller knows which block each value sat in). For exact per-reference attribution use `texts`, where each block names its own artifact. Never parsed out of the text. Ignored when `text` is empty — ids that name no content are not published as sources.
attached_artifact_ids.title: Attached Artifact Ids

files.description: Uploaded artifacts as base64-encoded bytes: PDF (text layer), Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx), Excel/CSV, EML, HTML, nmap/Nessus XML, STIX/SBOM/SARIF/MISP JSON, or any text. Parsed by format and combined with `text`. Images and scanned PDFs are not read. Up to 20 files per enrichment.
files.title: Files

formats.description: Export formats to serialize from the assembled report. Options: report, json (raw ArtifactEnrichmentReport), stix (2.1 bundle), vex (OpenVEX), csaf (CSAF 2.0 VEX), navigator (ATT&CK Navigator v4.5 layer), kev_remediation, oscal_poam, misp (event JSON), csv.
formats.title: Formats

include.description: Report sections to include. Replaces the default list. Allowed values: attack_paths, citations, defenses, enrichment, narrative, rollups, source_corroboration. Core decisions, scores, grades, and prioritized actions are always returned.
include.title: Include

stakeholder.description: Deployment context for the SSVC decision (system exposure + impact). Optional — defaults to a conservative worst-reasonable case (open / medium) when omitted.

text.description: Pasted text — an IR note, advisory, or raw indicators. References are extracted automatically. Use `texts` instead when the content came from more than one artifact, so each reference can be attributed to the artifact it actually appeared in.
examples: CVE-2024-3400 is under active exploitation; C2 at evil-c2.com
text.title: Text

texts.description: Structured text blocks, each optionally naming the artifact it came from. Combined with the legacy `text` field and `files`; every block is its own source, so a reference found in one block is attributed to that block's `source_artifact_id` and a reference found in several carries all of their ids. Up to 20 blocks; the aggregate of `text` + `texts[].text` is capped.
texts.title: Texts

tlp.description: TLP 2.0 sharing marking stamped into every requested export that has a slot for one: CLEAR, GREEN, AMBER, AMBER+STRICT or RED. Omit it and the run uses YOUR saved default for the Artifact Enricher (GET/PUT /artifact-manager/settings, `artifact_tlp`), which is AMBER until you set one — an export can carry customer input, so nothing is marked CLEAR unless you choose it. An explicit `tlp` always wins over the saved default. CSAF 2.0 only accepts TLP 1.0 labels, so CLEAR is written as WHITE and AMBER+STRICT as AMBER plus a distribution note. STIX 2.1 gets the official TLP 2.0 marking-definition on every object, MISP a `tlp:*` event tag, Navigator a `TLP` metadata entry, OSCAL a `tlp` metadata prop, and the human report and KEV worksheet (both Crimson wrapper dicts) a top-level `tlp` label — the KEV worksheet's rows stay CISA-verbatim and the raw `json` pass-through is unmarked. OpenVEX (closed schema) and CSV (fixed column contract) have no marking slot and stay unmarked.
tlp.title: Tlp

Defaults represent a conservative unknown environment: ``exposure=open`` and
``human_impact=medium``. ``method`` selects the CERT/CC Deployer tree (default) or the CISA
Coordinator tree. ``human_impact`` applies to the Deployer tree; ``mission_prevalence`` and
``public_wellbeing_impact`` apply to the Coordinator tree.

ArtifactTextInput.description:
One block of pasted/forwarded text, with the artifact it came from when the caller knows it.

The structured counterpart to the legacy scalar ``text`` / ``attachments_text``. Each entry is
its own source: its ``source_artifact_id`` (when set) attributes every reference extracted from
THAT block to that artifact, and a block with no id is unnamed — it is never attributed to some
other entry's artifact. This is what makes multi-artifact attribution exact: a value found in

include.description: Response layers to include. Replaces the default list. Allowed values: affected_products, campaigns, capec, cisa_kev, criteria, cwe, defend, details, detections, epss, exploits, groups, inferred_chain, kev, knowledgebase, log_sources, metasploit, misp, mitigations, navigator, nist_controls, nuclei, osv, osv_restricted, poc, poc_source, similar_cves, software, ssvc, summary, techniques, tie, timeline, vendor_advisories, distro_advisories, versions, affected_chipsets, android_bulletin, cellular, cellular_core, cvss_bt, emb3d, sigma, vulnrichment, euvd, vince, csaf_advisories, certfr_advisories, jvn, ot_vendor_advisories, weakness_ranks. `capec_full`, `csaf_advisories_full`, and `certfr_advisories_full` restore full CVE rows; the advisory summaries retain at most 10 newest rows and omit large fields. `versions` attaches the object's KB revision history (`revision_history`). `cisa_kev` is included by default and reads the stored CISA catalog for this CVE, filling the `kev` columns the mirror cannot carry (`vendor_project`, `product`, `forensic_triage`) or left empty (`notes`), marking the entry `supplemented_from='cisa-official'`; a CVE the mirror does not carry gets a `kev` entry built from CISA's own record, so it does not need `kev` in the same request. `metasploit` and `nuclei` use stored catalogs. Along with `vendor_advisories`, they have separate response blocks (`metasploit_modules`, `nuclei_templates`, `vendor_advisories`); none feeds the offline authoritative path or the weaponization score. These layers are optional on this endpoint; artifact and inventory enrichment can add `metasploit` and `nuclei` automatically. `distro_advisories` adds stored SUSE CSAF-VEX, Ubuntu OpenVEX and Alpine secdb rows for this CVE, one per release (fixed / not_affected / needs_triage / open), each with its licence and attribution. Debian is not included. It does not feed the offline path. `distro_advisories_totals` (rows per source before the 200-row cap) and `distro_advisories_truncated` say what the cap cut. `criteria` resolves distinct `match_criteria_id` on the affected-product rows into the NVD criterion it names — its matchstring, version-range bounds, covered software and the CVEs it hits, plus its revision timestamps — so the join key that endpoint publishes resolves in the other direction; it loads those rows for itself, so it does not need `affected_products` in the same request (and does not publish that layer). `details` does not gate this endpoint's own `cve` object — it is returned whether or not the token is requested (the token still counts toward the include set `confidence` reports). The technique-derived layers (`groups`, `software`, `campaigns`, `mitigations`, `detections`, `defend`, `navigator`, `nist_controls`, `tie`) resolve the technique set they read, so they answer without `techniques` in the same request — and they never publish it: `techniques[]` still requires its own token. `timeline` reads the same EPSS series as `epss` and does not publish the `epss` object either. `cellular_core` returns the RANsacked research page's row for this CVE — the affected cellular-core implementation with its LTE/5G qualifier, from the curated 73-CVE table (`cellular_core_entries[]`); it is deliberately separate from `cellular`, which is the Zenodo 5G dataset with its own tags. `certfr_advisories` returns the CERT-FR (ANSSI) avis and alertes that reference this CVE, with the reference id, title, last revision date, canonical page URL, the advisory's own `scada` flag, affected vendors/products and its published risk descriptions (`certfr_advisories[]`); link and metadata only. `jvn` returns the JVNDB advisories that reference this CVE, as link and metadata rows (`jvn_advisories[]`); the advisory body is never redistributed. `ot_vendor_advisories` returns the direct OT/embedded vendor advisories that name this CVE — Rockwell Automation and MediaTek, with CVE ids, CVSS scores and MediaTek chipset codes (`ot_vendor_advisories[]`); a seeded in-process corpus, link and metadata only. `cisa_campaigns` returns the CISA joint cybersecurity advisories (AA-series) whose STIX bundle references this CVE, as bounded metadata plus context (`cisa_campaigns[]`: advisory id, title, published date, URL, sectors, locations, threat actors, ATT&CK techniques and the bundle's observable count); the advisory body is never redistributed. `defend` reaches its countermeasures through the technique's ATT&CK mitigations — the corpus links D3FEND to mitigations, never directly to a technique — and reports `error: "no_mapping"` only where that join finds none. `ot_context` attaches the OT/RF block: `sectors[]` (the ICS Advisory Project CSV, CSAF notes, then a curated vendor map, each row naming its source), `protocols[]` and `rf_technology[]` from CPE/product/CSAF/Nuclei text, `fix_availability` from CSAF product status, `kev_ot` from the KEV vendor, `access_vector_rf` from the CVSS access vector, and the CVE's ISA/IEC 62443 requirements. It is a deterministic zero-LLM derivation; it reads the cached Vulmatch `cve_bundle_software` rows and the CSAF table when requested alone, and adds no new external source. It also extends `weakness_ranks` with `ics_weakness[]` (CWE-1358) and `iec_62443_requirements[]` (CWE-1424), which the `weakness_ranks` token itself also returns.

techniques_scope.description:
Precision filter for the resolved `techniques`. Trades recall against CVE-specificity:
- `all` (default): every linked technique, including those derived from broad/Pillar CWEs (e.g. CWE-20 'Improper Input Validation'). Maximum recall, but unrelated CVEs sharing a generic CWE converge on the same coarse set — check `techniques_provenance` to tell which.
- `specific`: drop techniques attributable only to a generic CWE's CAPEC closure, keeping those tied to the CVE's specific weaknesses. Higher precision; may be empty when the CVE has no specific ATT&CK mapping (the honest answer for such CVEs).
Ignored when `techniques` is not in `include`.

include.description: Response layers to include. Replaces the default list. Allowed values: analytic_details, asset_classes, atomic_red_team, campaigns, cisa_campaigns, cves, defend, details, detections, fight, framework_mappings, fraud, groups, knowledgebase, log_sources, lolbas, lotl, misp, mitigations, navigator, nist_controls, sigma, software, summary, tie, versions. `versions` attaches the object's KB revision history (`revision_history`). `analytic_details` attaches each detection analytic's tunable fields and log sources. `fraud` attaches `f3_techniques` — the MITRE F3 fraud techniques sharing this technique's own ATT&CK id. `asset_classes` attaches `asset_classes[]` — the ICS asset classes this technique targets, on an `ics` framework request. `sigma` attaches `sigma_rules[]` — the SigmaHQ detection rules whose ATT&CK tags name this technique (DRL-1.1). `lotl` attaches `lol_drivers[]` (the LOLDrivers entries exercising this technique), `gtfobins_binaries[]` (GTFOBins tools whose functions/contexts map onto it) and `hijacklibs_entries[]` (HijackLibs DLL hijacks whose type maps onto it) — facts only, joined through the committed function/type → ATT&CK map, never by name. Each source is capped at 50 rows per technique; `lol_drivers_total`, `gtfobins_binaries_total` and `hijacklibs_entries_total` carry the true counts. `fight` attaches `fight_techniques[]` — the MITRE FiGHT 5G techniques whose own `FGT` id maps onto this ATT&CK id (id-only join, never name matching; FiGHT-specific sub-techniques with no ATT&CK parent answer nothing). `lolbas` attaches `lolbas_binaries[]` — the LOLBAS binaries whose commands declare this ATT&CK technique, as names and ids only (no commands or descriptions). `framework_mappings` attaches `framework_mappings[]` — the CTID control/capability mappings for this technique across the aws, azure, gcp, m365, csa_ccm, veris, cri_profile, intel-vpro and cis frameworks; each row carries its own ATT&CK version because the families were built against different ones. `cisa_campaigns` attaches `cisa_campaigns[]` — the CISA joint cybersecurity advisories (AA-series) whose STIX bundle names this technique (a parent technique also matches advisories naming one of its sub-techniques), with their actors, sectors, locations and observable count. `atomic_red_team` attaches `atomic_tests[]` — the Red Canary Atomic Red Team tests exercising this technique (a parent also matches its sub-techniques), first 50 per technique with `atomic_tests_total` carrying the true count; each row carries the test name, auto_generated_guid, supported platforms, executor name, elevation flag and the upstream YAML link, never a command body.

CoverageGap.description:
Structured "what we DON'T know" entry surfaced at the report root.

Each kind is a pure derivation from existing structured fields on the references — no
invented signals. Analysts must see coverage gaps before they trust the report; this

EnrichCVERequest.description: Enrich a CVE with severity, exploit intelligence, attack patterns, and AI analysis.

include.description: Response layers to include. Replaces the default list. Allowed values: affected_products, campaigns, capec, cisa_kev, criteria, cwe, defend, details, detections, epss, exploits, groups, inferred_chain, kev, knowledgebase, log_sources, metasploit, misp, mitigations, navigator, nist_controls, nuclei, osv, osv_restricted, poc, poc_source, similar_cves, software, ssvc, summary, techniques, tie, timeline, vendor_advisories, distro_advisories, versions, affected_chipsets, android_bulletin, cellular, cellular_core, cvss_bt, emb3d, sigma, vulnrichment, euvd, vince, csaf_advisories, certfr_advisories, jvn, ot_vendor_advisories, weakness_ranks. `capec_full`, `csaf_advisories_full`, and `certfr_advisories_full` restore full CVE rows; the advisory summaries retain at most 10 newest rows and omit large fields. `versions` attaches the object's KB revision history (`revision_history`). `cisa_kev` is included by default and reads the stored CISA catalog for this CVE, filling the `kev` columns the mirror cannot carry (`vendor_project`, `product`, `forensic_triage`) or left empty (`notes`), marking the entry `supplemented_from='cisa-official'`; a CVE the mirror does not carry gets a `kev` entry built from CISA's own record, so it does not need `kev` in the same request. `metasploit` and `nuclei` use stored catalogs. Along with `vendor_advisories`, they have separate response blocks (`metasploit_modules`, `nuclei_templates`, `vendor_advisories`); none feeds the offline authoritative path or the weaponization score. These layers are optional on this endpoint; artifact and inventory enrichment can add `metasploit` and `nuclei` automatically. `distro_advisories` adds stored SUSE CSAF-VEX, Ubuntu OpenVEX and Alpine secdb rows for this CVE, one per release (fixed / not_affected / needs_triage / open), each with its licence and attribution. Debian is not included. It does not feed the offline path. `distro_advisories_totals` (rows per source before the 200-row cap) and `distro_advisories_truncated` say what the cap cut. `criteria` resolves distinct `match_criteria_id` on the affected-product rows into the NVD criterion it names — its matchstring, version-range bounds, covered software and the CVEs it hits, plus its revision timestamps — so the join key that endpoint publishes resolves in the other direction; it loads those rows for itself, so it does not need `affected_products` in the same request (and does not publish that layer). `details` does not gate this endpoint's own `cve` object — it is returned whether or not the token is requested (the token still counts toward the include set `confidence` reports). The technique-derived layers (`groups`, `software`, `campaigns`, `mitigations`, `detections`, `defend`, `navigator`, `nist_controls`, `tie`) resolve the technique set they read, so they answer without `techniques` in the same request — and they never publish it: `techniques[]` still requires its own token. `timeline` reads the same EPSS series as `epss` and does not publish the `epss` object either. `cellular_core` returns the RANsacked research page's row for this CVE — the affected cellular-core implementation with its LTE/5G qualifier, from the curated 73-CVE table (`cellular_core_entries[]`); it is deliberately separate from `cellular`, which is the Zenodo 5G dataset with its own tags. `certfr_advisories` returns the CERT-FR (ANSSI) avis and alertes that reference this CVE, with the reference id, title, last revision date, canonical page URL, the advisory's own `scada` flag, affected vendors/products and its published risk descriptions (`certfr_advisories[]`); link and metadata only. `jvn` returns the JVNDB advisories that reference this CVE, as link and metadata rows (`jvn_advisories[]`); the advisory body is never redistributed. `ot_vendor_advisories` returns the direct OT/embedded vendor advisories that name this CVE — Rockwell Automation and MediaTek, with CVE ids, CVSS scores and MediaTek chipset codes (`ot_vendor_advisories[]`); a seeded in-process corpus, link and metadata only. `cisa_campaigns` returns the CISA joint cybersecurity advisories (AA-series) whose STIX bundle references this CVE, as bounded metadata plus context (`cisa_campaigns[]`: advisory id, title, published date, URL, sectors, locations, threat actors, ATT&CK techniques and the bundle's observable count); the advisory body is never redistributed. `defend` reaches its countermeasures through the technique's ATT&CK mitigations — the corpus links D3FEND to mitigations, never directly to a technique — and reports `error: "no_mapping"` only where that join finds none. `ot_context` attaches the OT/RF block: `sectors[]` (the ICS Advisory Project CSV, CSAF notes, then a curated vendor map, each row naming its source), `protocols[]` and `rf_technology[]` from CPE/product/CSAF/Nuclei text, `fix_availability` from CSAF product status, `kev_ot` from the KEV vendor, `access_vector_rf` from the CVSS access vector, and the CVE's ISA/IEC 62443 requirements. It is a deterministic zero-LLM derivation; it reads the cached Vulmatch `cve_bundle_software` rows and the CSAF table when requested alone, and adds no new external source. It also extends `weakness_ranks` with `ics_weakness[]` (CWE-1358) and `iec_62443_requirements[]` (CWE-1424), which the `weakness_ranks` token itself also returns.

Ignored when `ssvc` is not in `include`.

techniques_scope.description:
Precision filter for the resolved `techniques`. Trades recall against CVE-specificity:
- `all` (default): every linked technique, including those derived from broad/Pillar CWEs (e.g. CWE-20 'Improper Input Validation'). Maximum recall, but unrelated CVEs sharing a generic CWE converge on the same coarse set — check `techniques_provenance` to tell which.
- `specific`: drop techniques attributable only to a generic CWE's CAPEC closure, keeping those tied to the CVE's specific weaknesses. Higher precision; may be empty when the CVE has no specific ATT&CK mapping (the honest answer for such CVEs).
Ignored when `techniques` is not in `include`.

EnrichCWERequest.description:
Enrich a weakness classification with linked attack patterns and their ATT&CK mappings.

Techniques resolve from this weakness's CAPEC links, so the layer is only as complete as those
links are: a CAPEC carrying no ATT&CK mapping contributes none, and the layers derived from
techniques are empty with it. Some weaknesses carry no CAPECs at all.
Supply at least one of `cwe_id` or `search`.

cwe_id.description: CWE identifier (e.g. CWE-79). Supply this or `search`.
cwe_id.title: Cwe Id

include.description: Response layers to include. Replaces the default list. Allowed values: campaigns, capecs, cves, defend, details, detections, groups, knowledgebase, log_sources, mitigations, navigator, nist_controls, software, summary, techniques, tie, versions. `versions` attaches the object's KB revision history (`revision_history`). `details` does not gate this endpoint's own `weakness` object — it is returned whether or not the token is requested (the token still counts toward the include set `confidence` reports). The CAPEC rows behind the technique-derived layers resolve for those tokens themselves — `groups`, `software`, `campaigns`, `mitigations`, `detections`, `defend`, `navigator`, `nist_controls` and `tie` answer without `capecs` or `techniques` in the same request, and `capecs` / `techniques` are still what PUBLISH their own sections. `defend` reaches its countermeasures through the technique's ATT&CK mitigations — the corpus links D3FEND to mitigations, never directly to a technique — and reports `error: "no_mapping"` only where that join finds none.
include.title: Include

search.description: Text query to discover weaknesses by name or description (e.g. 'Cross-site Scripting') — the discovery path CWE was missing while CAPEC/F3/CLOAK all had one. Supply this or `cwe_id`.
search.title: Search

include.description: Response layers to include. Replaces the default list. Allowed values: analytic_details, campaigns, cisa_campaigns, cves, defend, detections, domain_context, galaxies, galaxy_clusters_full, groups, hashlookup, inferred_chain, knowledgebase, listed_on, log_sources, misp_attributes, mitigations, navigator, network_context, nist_controls, poc, sightings, software, summary, techniques, tie, warninglist. `galaxy_clusters_full` returns cluster profiles with inbound relations; the 30-cluster fetch cap remains. `network_context` adds ASN / AS name / registration country / covering prefix from the seeded iptoasn corpus (IP values only). `domain_context` adds RDAP registration facts (registration and expiry dates, age in days, registrar, status) for a domain, hostname, or the host of a URL. `listed_on` unifies every list hit into one ledger — curated MISP feed caches plus the seeded Spamhaus DROP / ASN-DROP corpora — and is the only field that can report a `cidr` or `asn` match. `analytic_details` attaches each detection analytic's tunable fields and log sources. The technique-derived layers (analytic_details, campaigns, defend, detections, groups, log_sources, mitigations, navigator, nist_controls, software, techniques, tie) read the MISP attributes' galaxy tags, so each resolves that read for itself and answers without `misp_attributes` in the same request — while `misp_attributes` is still what publishes that section. `defend` reaches its countermeasures through the technique's ATT&CK mitigations — the corpus links D3FEND to mitigations, never directly to a technique — and reports `error: "no_mapping"` only where that join finds none. `hashlookup` attaches `hashlookup` — the CIRCL hashlookup / NSRL known-good verdict — and is answered only for the hash types (md5, sha1, sha256); every other type returns null and makes no request. `cisa_campaigns` attaches `cisa_campaigns[]` — the CISA joint cybersecurity advisories (AA-series) whose STIX bundle publishes this indicator, each carrying the matching observables in `matched_indicators`; matching is on the normalised observable type (`ip-src`/`ip-dst`/`ip` → IPv4/IPv6, `hostname` → domain, case-insensitive hashes and domains) and is exact, never a substring or a URL host of a domain.

type.description: Indicator type. Common values: ip-dst, ip-src, domain, hostname, md5, sha1, sha256, url, email. `ip-src` and `ip-dst` both search BOTH IP directions — an address is one indicator however the source labelled it — and `ip` is an alias for that same both-direction search. Which directions matched is reported as `matched_value_types`.
type.title: Type

value.description: Indicator value (IP address, hash, domain, etc.)
value.title: Value

EnrichPackageRequest.description:
Find vulnerabilities affecting an open-source package in the stored OSV corpus.

Keyed by package **ecosystem + name (+ optional version)** — the dependency-vuln
surface (npm / PyPI / Go / Maven / crates.io / …) that the CPE-keyed `enrich/product`
can't reach. With a version, results are filtered to advisories whose affected ranges
include it; without one, eligible advisories for the package are paged without version filtering.

ecosystem.description: Package ecosystem. Common loose spellings are normalized to OSV's canonical form (e.g. 'pypi' → 'PyPI', 'cargo' → 'crates.io', 'go' → 'Go'); unrecognized values (incl. distro ecosystems like 'Debian') pass through verbatim.
ecosystem.title: Ecosystem

include.description: OSV advisory sections and nested CVE enrichment layers. Replaces the default list. Allowed values: affected, affected_products, campaigns, capec, cisa_kev, criteria, cwe, defend, details, detections, epss, exploits, groups, inferred_chain, kev, knowledgebase, log_sources, metasploit, misp, mitigations, navigator, nist_controls, nuclei, osv, osv_restricted, poc, poc_source, references, severity, similar_cves, software, ssvc, summary, techniques, tie, timeline, vendor_advisories, versions, affected_chipsets, csaf_advisories, cvss_bt, emb3d, sigma, vulnrichment, weakness_ranks, cellular_core, certfr_advisories, jvn, ot_vendor_advisories. `capec_full`, `csaf_advisories_full`, and `certfr_advisories_full` restore nested CVE rows. `vince`, `euvd`, `android_bulletin` and `cellular` are single-CVE-only sources and are rejected here: this endpoint fans out to every CVE the advisories alias. `osv_restricted` adds restricted and unknown-licence package and nested CVE advisories. `severity`, `affected`, and `references` choose the OSV advisory sections; every other layer is applied to each CVE the advisories alias to (`details` does both — it gates the advisory text and rides the per-CVE chain). `cisa_kev`, `criteria`, `metasploit`, `nuclei` and `vendor_advisories` are forwarded to that per-CVE chain as separate nested blocks. CISA KEV uses a stored catalog and contributes to KEV-derived scores; the other layers do not feed the offline authoritative path or the weaponization score. Advisory IDs, aliases, summaries, and fixed versions are always returned. `ot_context` is forwarded to each nested CVE (OT/RF context derived without a new upstream source).

EnrichProductRequest.description: Find vulnerabilities affecting a specific product and enrich each CVE.

include.description: Layers to include for each matched CVE. Replaces the default list. Allowed values: affected_products, campaigns, capec, cisa_kev, cwe, defend, details, detections, epss, exploits, groups, kev, knowledgebase, log_sources, metasploit, misp, mitigations, navigator, nist_controls, nuclei, osv, osv_restricted, poc, risk_summary, software, ssvc, summary, techniques, tie, lifecycle, cvss_bt, vulnrichment, cellular_core, certfr_advisories, jvn, ot_vendor_advisories, weakness_ranks, emb3d, csaf_advisories. `capec_full` and `certfr_advisories_full` restore nested CVE rows; `csaf_advisories_full` also restores complete product-level CSAF rows. `csaf_advisories_total` and `csaf_advisories_truncated` report the product-level summary cap. For full log sources, PoCs, Sigma rules, or D3FEND rows, call enrich/cve with the CVE ID, `techniques`, the base layer, and its `log_sources_full`, `poc_full`, `sigma_full`, or `defend_full` token. `lifecycle` attaches the product-level `lifecycle` block (endoflife.date); `cvss_bt` and `vulnrichment` are per-CVE layers forwarded to each matched CVE; `cellular_core`, `certfr_advisories`, `jvn` and `ot_vendor_advisories` are zero-cost in-process layers forwarded the same way. `details` does not gate this endpoint's own `product` object, its discovered CVEs, or the per-CVE fan-out — all are returned whether or not the token is requested (the token still counts toward the include set `confidence` reports). The technique-derived per-CVE layers (`groups`, `software`, `campaigns`, `mitigations`, `detections`, `defend`, `navigator`, `nist_controls`, `tie`) resolve the technique set they read, so they answer without `techniques` in the same request and never publish it. The product-level `nist_controls` rollup reads the nested rows' `techniques[]`, so it resolves them for the rollup and clears them again when the outer request did not `defend` reaches its countermeasures through the technique's ATT&CK mitigations — the corpus links D3FEND to mitigations, never directly to a technique — and reports `error: "no_mapping"` only where that join finds none. `ot_context` attaches the product-level OT/RF block and is forwarded to each nested CVE (so those rows carry their own `ot_context` too); it reads the cached Vulmatch software rows and the CSAF table when requested alone; `lifecycle` also fills its `fix_availability.eol`.

product.description: Product name to search. Spaces and capitalization are normalized for CPE matching. Use the canonical CPE product name — `http_server`, not `Apache httpd`. A human-style name that normalizes to no CPE (`Apache httpd` -> `apache_httpd`) returns an empty result set, so prefer the CPE form and pass the vendor separately: `http_server` + `vendor: apache` is the highest-yield shape.

Zero matches returns an empty CVE set plus a 'version_filter'/'no_match' marker in errors[] — never a silent fallback to unfiltered. When no matched CVE states a version for the product, the supplied version narrows nothing: errors[] carries 'version_filter'/'version_not_applied' instead, naming the product when no matched CPE lists the version at all.

EventEnrichmentRequest.description:
Event Enricher — submit a raw security/log event for async indicator enrichment.

The reactive (event-driven) counterpart to the Artifact + Inventory Enrichers: hand it a raw
security event (a Defender XDR / Sentinel alert, a SIEM/EDR log line, any JSON or text) and the
enrichment runs in the background — it extracts the indicators (CVEs / ATT&CK techniques / IOCs /
products) the same deterministic way the Artifact Enricher does, enriches each against the
authoritative CTI sources, and aggregates a per-event threat verdict. A SOC platform submits an
alert here instead of looping the single `/v1/enrich/*` endpoints itself.

event.description: The raw event — a Defender/Sentinel alert JSON, a log line, or any text. Indicators are extracted server-side (callers stringify structured events).
event.title: Event

EventEnrichmentRequest.title: EventEnrichmentRequest

EventEnrichmentResult.description:
Event Enrichment result — per-indicator enrichment + an aggregate event threat assessment.

The payload stored on the async job object's ``result`` and returned by the poll endpoint when
the enrichment is ``done``. It is NOT persisted anywhere else: the engine is stateless by
decision (#358, closed 2026-09-08 — no consumer, and raw SOC events are too sensitive to hold
for nobody). The ``event_enrichment`` ``ArtifactKind`` exists (migration 022) but nothing writes
it. The caller keeps the polled result.

InvalidBatchItem.description:
A batch item that no supported enrich type accepted.

Kept as a member of the request union so ONE malformed item is answered per-item — a
`status="error"` result naming what failed — instead of rejecting the whole request with a 422.
That is the same partial-failure shape `BatchItemResult` already documents for dispatch
failures, and it is what the endpoint's contract ("one item failing does not fail the batch")
requires: a single typo in item 50 of a 50-item batch must not discard the other 49. The item's
fields are preserved verbatim so the route can report the validator's own message for it.

InventoryEnrichmentRequest.description:
Submit product and package assets for asynchronous CVE findings and a portfolio rollup.

Product assets use CPE matching. Assets with `ecosystem` set use package-advisory matching.
Each asset can carry deployment and ownership context, which is preserved in the result.
An optional `vex_overlay` carries VEX statements (OpenVEX 0.2.0 / CSAF 2.0) that mark matching
`not_affected` / `fixed` findings `suppressed_by_vex` — retained with their justification, excluded
from the actionable counts — instead of re-reporting them.

attached_artifact_ids.description: LEGACY whole-run provenance: the ids of the stored artifacts whose content is in the legacy scalar `attachments_text`. Recorded on the attachment report's `attachment_sources` (kind `text`), and every reference extracted from that text carries all of them. For exact per-reference attribution use `attachments_texts`, where each block names its own artifact. Ignored when `attachments_text` is empty.
attached_artifact_ids.title: Attached Artifact Ids

attachments_files.description: Optional attached files as base64-encoded bytes. Supports the same formats as Artifact Enrichment (PDF (text layer), Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx), Excel/CSV, EML, HTML, nmap/Nessus XML, STIX/SBOM/SARIF/MISP JSON, or any text) and combines them with `attachments_text`. Maximum 20 files.
attachments_files.title: Attachments Files

attachments_text.description: Optional text extracted from artifacts attached to the inventory, such as reports, IOC lists, or prior enrichments. When present, the Artifact Enricher analyzes it and returns the report in `result.attachment_enrichment`. Maximum 500,000 characters. Name the artifacts the text came from in `attached_artifact_ids` and the report records them as its sources — attribution is read from that field only, never guessed from the text.
attachments_text.title: Attachments Text

attachments_texts.description: Structured attachment text blocks, each optionally naming the artifact it came from. Use this instead of the legacy scalar `attachments_text` when the content came from more than one artifact: every block is its own source, so a reference found in one block is attributed to that block's `source_artifact_id` and a reference found in several carries all of their ids. Combined with `attachments_text` and `attachments_files`; the aggregate of `attachments_text` + `attachments_texts[].text` is capped.
attachments_texts.title: Attachments Texts

include.description: Per-asset CVE layers to include. Omit it for **every layer the product route accepts** minus the reasoned exclusions; optional public metadata follows the deployment setting. Pass a list to narrow it. Allowed values: affected_products, campaigns, capec, cisa_kev, cwe, defend, details, detections, epss, exploits, groups, kev, knowledgebase, log_sources, metasploit, misp, mitigations, navigator, nist_controls, nuclei, osv, osv_restricted, poc, risk_summary, software, ssvc, summary, techniques, tie, lifecycle, cvss_bt, vulnrichment, cellular_core, certfr_advisories, jvn, ot_vendor_advisories, weakness_ranks, emb3d, csaf_advisories. `capec_full`, `csaf_advisories_full`, and `certfr_advisories_full` request full nested CVE rows. For full log sources, PoCs, Sigma rules, or D3FEND rows, call enrich/cve with the CVE ID, `techniques`, the base layer, and its `log_sources_full`, `poc_full`, `sigma_full`, or `defend_full` token. Summary and navigator are accepted for product compatibility but omitted by Inventory Enrichment. When the deployment enables public metadata (`ENRICH_PUBLIC_METADATA`, on by default), cisa_kev, metasploit, and nuclei are added automatically. `ot_context` adds the per-CVE OT/RF block (sectors, protocols, fix availability, KEV-OT, RF technology, 62443).
include.title: Include

items.description: Assets to enrich (1-1000, of which at most 200 product assets without an `ecosystem`). Each asset may carry one version or up to five versions; findings for the same asset are combined. Larger inventories take longer to finish.
items.title: Items

vex_overlay.description: Optional VEX suppression overlay (OpenVEX 0.2.0 or CSAF 2.0 VEX JSON). Statements that are `not_affected`/`known_not_affected`/`fixed` for a CVE on one of the submitted assets' own CPE identifiers mark that finding `suppressed_by_vex` in the result — retained, labeled with the statement's justification, and excluded from the actionable posture counts. `affected`/`under_investigation` statements never suppress. The enricher's own OpenVEX/CSAF exports re-ingest: flip a statement to `not_affected`/`fixed` and submit it back.

Null on nearly every row: the shipped CTID mapping carries a non-empty `comments` value on 4 of its 5,314 `mitigates` entries, so only four (control, technique) pairs ever carry one — CM-03/T1666, AC-02/T1556.009, SI-03/T1027.013 and SI-03/T1027.014 (measured 2026-09-13). SearchMISPRequest.description:
Search our curated MISP (public threat feeds) by indicator value, event info, or event ID.

Attribute filters (`value`, `type_attribute`, `category`, `tags`, `to_ids`) search attributes;
event filters (`eventinfo`, `published`) search events; `event_id` looks one event up directly.
The threat-level and date filters apply to BOTH kinds, so a request carrying only those —
with no attribute, event, or event-ID selector — searches attributes and events.

Otherwise events are summary rows. The default is `event_reports`, `tags`, and `version`; pass `include=[]` to skip them. Allowed values: event_reports, feeds, misp_events_full, objects, sightings, stats, tags, version.

Two modes on one surface: pass `vendor` for that vendor's product catalogue; omit it (optionally

info.description:
Turn a CVE, IOC, product, package, weakness, or ATT&CK entity into a response you can
use in a ticket, report, or agent workflow. The API returns severity, exploit evidence, weakness analysis,
ATT&CK mappings, defensive guidance, and prioritization data.

This reference covers 38 operations: 32 synchronous enrichment, search, and assessment endpoints, plus
6 async submit and status operations.

## Make your first request

```bash
curl -X POST https://crimsoncrawler.com/v1/enrich/cve \
  -H "apikey: YOUR_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cve_id": "CVE-2024-3400"}'
```

The default CVE response includes details, EPSS, KEV, weaknesses, attack patterns, ATT&CK techniques,
technique predictions, and NIST controls.

## Choose an endpoint

| Category | Operations | Use it for |
|---|---:|---|
| Enrichment | 19 | Resolve 1 entity, or enrich up to 50 mixed items with `/v1/enrich/batch`. |
| Search | 9 | Find CVEs, threat records, known-exploited vulnerabilities, vendors, and public exploit material. |
| Assessment | 4 | Compare technique coverage, vulnerability exposure, group exposure, or an IOC portfolio. |
| Async enrichment | 6 | Submit text, files, an asset inventory, or one raw event, then poll for the report. |

## Control response depth

Most enrichment endpoints, every assessment endpoint, and `/v1/search/cve` accept `include`. Passing it
selects the exact response layers and replaces that endpoint's default set.

```json
{
  "cve_id": "CVE-2024-3400",
  "include": ["details", "epss", "kev", "techniques", "ssvc", "summary"]
}
```

Requesting fewer layers is usually faster. Each billable v1 call still consumes 1 request unit, regardless of depth.

## Read the response

Fields excluded by `include` return as `null` or empty arrays. If requested intelligence is unavailable,
a `200` response keeps the data that resolved and records the gap in `errors[]`.

Common HTTP outcomes:

| Status | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| `200` | Synchronous request completed. Check `errors[]` for partial source failures. |
| `202` | Async enrichment accepted; poll the returned identifier. |
| `401` | API key is missing, invalid, or inactive. |
| `404` | Async identifier is missing, expired, or owned by another key. |
| `422` | Request shape, field value, or cross-field combination is invalid. |
| `429` | Gateway quota is exhausted, or an async key already has 20 jobs in flight. |
| `500` | An unexpected server error crossed the API's last-resort error boundary. |
| `503` | Async queue state could not be verified, so no job was accepted. |

Each operation below lists only the statuses it can return and its exact success schema.

## Run longer jobs

`POST /v1/artifact-enrich`, `POST /v1/inventory-enrich`, and `POST /v1/event-enrich` return `202` with an
`enrichment_id`. Poll the matching `GET /v1/*-enrich/{enrichment_id}` route until `status` is `done` or
`error`. Status polls consume no plan units. A submission consumes one plan unit when it is **accepted**;
a request the API refused (`429`, `503`) or rejected (`4xx`) consumes none.

Each key can run 3 async jobs at once and hold 20 running or queued jobs — enforced atomically, so
simultaneous submits from one key cannot exceed it. A full queue returns `429` with
`enrichment_queue_full`.

## Authenticate

Send your API key in the `apikey` header. `x-api-key` is also accepted. Keep keys out of source control,
URLs, request bodies, and browser-side code.

See [Quick Start](/docs/quickstart/) for a working integration, [Authentication](/docs/authentication/) for
limits and key rotation, and [Enrichment Depth](/docs/guides/enrichment-chains/) for endpoint-specific
`include` values.
info.title: Crimson Crawler API

post.description:
Submit security text or files for asynchronous Artifact Enrichment.

Returns an `enrichment_id` with HTTP 202. Poll
`/v1/artifact-enrich/{enrichment_id}` for stage progress and the finished report.

Supply up to 1,000,000 characters in `text`, up to 20 base64-encoded files, or both. Supported
inputs include scan exports, vulnerability reports, advisories, email, spreadsheets, and plain
text. The report resolves detected CVEs, products, packages, weaknesses, techniques, and
indicators into evidence, SSVC decisions, PATCH/BLOCK/WATCH/INFO actions, prioritized work,
attack paths, defensive guidance, citations, and requested machine-readable exports.

`include` selects report sections; it does not reduce the evidence used for core decisions.
Decisions, scores, grades, references, and prioritized actions are always returned. The allowed
section names and export formats are defined in the request schema.

`tlp` marks the exports that carry a marking. Omit it and the run uses your saved Artifact Enricher
default (`/artifact-manager/settings`); an explicit `tlp` always wins.

An ACCEPTED submission (202) consumes one request unit; a refused one (429/503) and every poll consume
none. Each API key can run 3 Artifact, Inventory, or Event Enrichments at once and can hold 20 running
or queued jobs across all three enrichment engines (the caps are shared, so the limit binds them
jointly). Jobs
beyond the running limit remain `queued`; a full queue returns 429, and that cap is enforced
atomically, so simultaneous submits cannot push an owner past it. If queue state cannot be
verified, the request returns 503 and no job is created.

Poll an Artifact Enrichment until it finishes.

Returns overall `progress`, ordered stage and substage progress, a rolling event feed, and one
of these states:

- `queued`: waiting for a slot; `queue_position` is the number of jobs ahead
- `running`: enrichment is in progress
- `done`: `result` contains the completed `ArtifactEnrichmentReport`
- `error`: `error` contains the terminal failure

Polling consumes no request units. Authenticated jobs are owner-gated: only the API-key owner
that submitted the job can read it, and a different key receives 404. Anonymous, keyless, and
direct MCP submissions use a capability URL, so possession of the job UUID is sufficient to
read the result. A missing, expired, malformed, or owner-hidden identifier returns 404 or 422.

post.description:
Analyze the aggregate technique surface across multiple CVEs.

Returns the combined, deduplicated ATT&CK technique surface with threat predictions. More
efficient than enriching CVEs individually when you need the aggregate picture.

**Include options**

- `techniques` *(default-on)* — deduplicated ATT&CK technique surface across the CVE set
- `tie` *(default-on)* — technique likelihood predictions
- `navigator` — ATT&CK Navigator layer JSON
- `defend` — D3FEND defensive techniques for the aggregate technique surface
- `exploit_chain` — CVEs grouped by ATT&CK kill-chain phase
- `prioritized_remediation` — CVEs in priority order with active-exploitation multipliers
  and compensating-controls downrank
- `remediation_plan` — deduplicated mitigations sorted by technique coverage
- `exploits` — confirmed exploit records from ExploitDB public exploit evidence across the
  assessed CVE set
- `osv` — OSV.dev advisories aliased to the assessed CVEs (GHSA/PYSEC/RUSTSEC records with
  per-ecosystem fixed versions), aggregated and deduplicated
- `summary` — AI-generated narrative of the aggregate attack-surface shape
- `nist_controls` *(default-on)* — NIST SP 800-53 rev 5 controls that mitigate the aggregate
  technique surface, based on MITRE Center for Threat-Informed Defense mappings
- `ssvc` — per-CVE SSVC decisions across the set (CERT/CC Deployer or CISA Coordinator);
  stakeholder context comes from the optional `stakeholder` request field, defaults apply when
  omitted (deployer / `exposure=open` / `human_impact=medium`)
- `csaf_advisories` *(default-on)* — CSAF vendor advisories naming any assessed CVE (CISA ICS,
  Siemens, Schneider, CERT@VDE members and the other allowlisted OT publishers), deduplicated,
  10 newest in summary form; `csaf_advisories_full` restores every row and field
- `ot_context` *(default-on)* — `ot_contexts[]`: per-CVE OT/RF context (sectors, protocols, fix
  availability, KEV-OT, RF technology, ISA/IEC 62443), the same block `enrich/cve` derives
- `certfr_advisories` — deduplicated CERT-FR advisories, capped at 10; `certfr_advisories_full`
  restores all rows and their CVE references
- `cisa_campaigns`, `emb3d` — deduplicated CISA advisories and embedded threats, capped at 10
- `jvn`, `ot_vendor_advisories` — opt-in JVN and direct OT vendor advisories, capped at 10
- `cellular`, `android_bulletin`, `cellular_core`, `affected_chipsets` — per-CVE cellular,
  Android and chipset data in `cve_ot_layers`; cellular-core and chipsets are opt-in

Several extra fields always populate: `weaponization_scores` (per-CVE — and the same score now
rides on each `cves[]` row, alongside its `poc_count`), `max_/avg_` rollups, `chained_cve_pairs`
(kill-chain adjacency plus vendor overlap), `likely_tactics` (union of vendor tactic-class hints
across the CVE set's affected products), and `kev_entries` for any KEV-listed CVE in the set,
for KEV-worksheet export. `kev_entries[]` carries `vulnerability_name`, `required_action`,
`notes`, `date_added`, `due_date` and `ransomware`; its `vendor_project`, `product` and
`short_description` come from the KEV object's `extensions` block, which the objects this
deployment serves do NOT carry (verified on both the CVE-bundle and `/v1/search/kev` paths,
2026-09-11), so those three arrive empty rather than absent.

OSV advisories are returned in budget-sized pages over the aggregated, deduplicated candidates of
every assessed CVE. When `osv_next_offset` is present, repeat the same request with `osv_offset` set
to it and `osv_snapshot_id` from the response until it is absent; each continuation page carries only
OSV advisories and errors. `osv_advisories_total` stays exact, a changed or expired snapshot returns
409 `snapshot_expired`, and an unreadable snapshot store or stored OSV copy returns 503
`snapshot_unavailable`.

post.description:
Batch-run multiple enrich/* lookups in one request, preserving input order.

Accepts 1-50 items; the 51st is rejected with HTTP 422. Each item carries a `type` discriminator
naming the enrichment type, that type's identifier fields, and its own per-type `include` list.
Each result follows the same response contract as its dedicated single-entity endpoint.

There is no batch-level `include` — each item drives its own enrichment depth via the include list
of the single-entity type it names. See that type's `/v1/enrich/*` endpoint for its include options.

**Supported types**

Each of the 18 maps 1:1 to a `/v1/enrich/*` endpoint:

- `cve`, `product`, `package`, `cwe`, `capec`, `technique`, `ioc`, `group`
- `software`, `campaign`, `atlas`, `disarm`, `f3`, `cloak`, `location`, `sector`, `defend`, `poc_source`

Partial failure is isolated: one item failing does not fail the batch. Each result reports
`status="ok"` (the enrichment ran — per-layer partial failures stay inside `data.errors`) or
`status="error"` (the item was rejected by validation, or its dispatch raised, with details in
the item's `errors`). An item that no supported type accepts — an unknown `type`, a missing or
invalid required field, or a non-object entry — is answered this way rather than with a 422, so
one malformed item never discards the batch's other results. Results preserve input order.

A batch consumes one request unit.

post.description:
Look up or search attack patterns and resolve their own ATT&CK mappings into techniques.

Provide `capec_id` for a direct lookup or `search` for text-based discovery. The ATT&CK techniques
linked to this attack pattern are resolved into full objects with mitigations and detection
guidance; a pattern carrying no ATT&CK mapping resolves to none, and the technique-derived
layers are empty with it.
If both fields are omitted, the endpoint returns HTTP 200 with no selected pattern and empty search results.

**Include options**

- `details` — full CAPEC object with description, prerequisites, and related weaknesses
- `techniques` — ATT&CK techniques linked to this attack pattern
- `tie` — technique likelihood predictions for linked techniques
- `navigator` — ATT&CK Navigator layer JSON for linked techniques
- `groups` — threat actor groups using the linked techniques
- `software` — malware and tools using the linked techniques
- `campaigns` — threat campaigns using the linked techniques
- `mitigations` — defensive courses of action per technique
- `detections` — detection data sources per technique
- `defend` — D3FEND defensive techniques and countermeasures
- `cves` — CVEs referencing this attack pattern (queried by CAPEC id, independent of the technique layer)
- `knowledgebase` — related intelligence from the knowledge base
- `summary` — AI-generated summary of the attack pattern
- `nist_controls` *(opt-in)* — NIST SP 800-53 rev 5 controls that mitigate the linked techniques,
  based on MITRE Center for Threat-Informed Defense mappings
- `network_context` *(opt-in)* — ASN, AS name, registration country and covering prefix for an IP
  indicator, from the seeded iptoasn corpus (PDDL v1.0). A registration country, not geolocation.
- `domain_context` *(opt-in)* — RDAP registration facts for a domain, hostname or the host of a URL:
  registration and expiration dates, domain age in days, registrar, registry and status codes.
- `listed_on` *(opt-in)* — every list carrying this value, unified across the curated MISP feed
  caches and the seeded Spamhaus DROP / ASN-DROP corpora, each entry naming how it matched
  (`exact`, `cidr`, or `asn`). MISP's own exact-value read is unchanged; CIDR and ASN matches are
  what an exact-value cache cannot express.

post.description:
Enrich a CVE into a full attack narrative.

Returns severity scoring, exploit intelligence, weakness analysis, adversary techniques,
threat predictions, and an AI-generated executive summary. Control depth with `include`.

ATT&CK mappings follow published CVE, CWE, and CAPEC relationships. If those relationships yield
no techniques, `techniques[]` stays empty rather than returning an unsupported match.

**Include options**

- `details` — core CVE data including CVSS, severity, description, dates, and references
- `epss` — EPSS exploit probability score and percentile ranking
- `kev` — Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog status
- `cisa_kev` — the stored CISA KEV catalog fills the `kev` entry columns the mirror
  cannot carry (`vendor_project`, `product`, `forensic_triage`) and marks it
  `supplemented_from='cisa-official'`; a CVE the mirror does not carry gets its entry from CISA.
- `versions` — KB revision history (`revision_history`) for the knowledge-base detail rows this
  response returns — the CWE weaknesses, CAPEC patterns and ATT&CK entities, each read from its
  own corpus and deduplicated per object. A request without the token reads no history at all
- `cwe` — root cause weakness classification with descriptions
- `capec` — attack patterns describing how the weakness is exploited
- `techniques` — ATT&CK techniques linked through published vulnerability relationships
- `tie` — technique likelihood predictions (probability per technique)
- `misp` — matching threat intelligence events from your threat feed
- `knowledgebase` — related context from the intelligence knowledge base
- `affected_products` — confirmed vulnerable software with vendor, product, version, and CPE string
- `criteria` *(opt-in)* — the NVD match criterion each `match_criteria_id` on
  `affected_products` names: its matchstring, version bounds, covered software and revision
  stamps. Loads the affected-product rows it reads for itself, and publishes none of them
- `poc` — proof-of-concept exploits from GitHub (count + repo metadata)
- `poc_source` — AI-assisted analysis of selected PoC repositories (trigger, affected path,
  preconditions, and mitigation); raw source code is never returned
- `exploits` — confirmed exploit records from ExploitDB public exploit evidence (real
  evidence, not the heuristic `has_public_exploit` boolean)
- `osv` — OSV.dev advisories aliased to this CVE (GHSA/PYSEC/RUSTSEC records plus per-ecosystem
  fixed versions; the same advisory source used by `/v1/enrich/package`)
- `groups` — threat actor groups known to use the linked ATT&CK techniques
- `software` — malware and tools that employ the linked techniques
- `campaigns` — threat campaigns that used the linked techniques
- `mitigations` — defensive courses of action for each linked technique
- `detections` — data sources and components for detecting each linked technique
- `defend` — D3FEND defensive techniques and countermeasures
- `metasploit` *(opt-in)* — `metasploit_modules`: Metasploit Framework modules naming this CVE
- `nuclei` *(opt-in)* — `nuclei_templates`: Nuclei templates naming this CVE (header fields only)
- `vendor_advisories` *(opt-in)* — `vendor_advisories`: Microsoft / Red Hat / Cisco advisory
  metadata for this CVE, one row per source that answered
- `distro_advisories` *(opt-in)* — `distro_advisories`: SUSE CSAF-VEX, Ubuntu OpenVEX and Alpine secdb rows
  per release (fixed / not_affected / needs_triage / open), each with its licence and attribution; Debian is absent
- `similar_cves` — up to 15 CVEs with overlapping weakness/technique fingerprint, ranked by
  weighted Jaccard similarity (signal-by-signal breakdown included)
- `timeline` — EPSS score history plus the derived `epss_velocity`; co-request `epss` and
  `timeline`, and both populate only when history is available
- `navigator` — ATT&CK Navigator layer JSON for MITRE's Navigator tool
- `summary` — AI-generated 3-5 sentence executive brief covering severity, exploitation
  status, and key attack techniques
- `inferred_chain` — quarantined AI-assisted technique candidates, returned only when published
  mappings yield no techniques. These low-confidence analyst hints are never treated as authoritative.
- `nist_controls` *(default-on)* — NIST SP 800-53 rev 5 controls that mitigate the CVE's mapped
  techniques, based on MITRE Center for Threat-Informed Defense mappings
- `weakness_ranks` *(opt-in)* — `weakness_ranks`: the CWE Top 25 and OWASP Top 10 / API / LLM
  positions this CVE's weakness ids occupy, matched by CWE id
- `ssvc` — SSVC vulnerability-prioritisation decision (CERT/CC Deployer tree by default, or CISA
  Coordinator tree). Stakeholder context comes from the optional `stakeholder` request field;
  defaults to the worst-reasonable case for an unknown environment.

Several extra fields always populate regardless of `include`: `techniques_provenance` (precision
class of `techniques[]`), `likely_tactics` (vendor tactic-class hints when the chain walk is
empty), `confidence` (importance-weighted completeness indicator), `weaponization_score` (0-100
composite).

The technique-derived layers — `groups`, `software`, `campaigns`, `mitigations`, `detections`,
`defend` and `nist_controls` — read the resolved technique set, which this endpoint resolves
itself (its chain walk plus its CAPEC links). Asked for ALONE each one resolves what it reads and
publishes only its own section, so `techniques[]` still requires its own token. Measured
2026-10-15: `["tie"]` alone → 20 predictions and `["timeline"]` alone → 72 EPSS points, both with
`techniques: []`.

OSV advisories are returned in budget-sized pages. When `osv_next_offset` is present, repeat the same
request with `osv_offset` set to it and `osv_snapshot_id` from the response until it is absent; each
continuation page carries only OSV advisories and errors. `osv_advisories_total` stays exact, a
changed or expired snapshot returns 409 `snapshot_expired`, and an unreadable snapshot store or
stored OSV copy returns 503 `snapshot_unavailable`.

post.description:
Enrich a weakness classification with linked attack patterns and their ATT&CK mappings.

Provide `cwe_id` for a direct lookup (e.g. CWE-79) or `search` for discovery by name; a request
naming neither is rejected with `422`.
Returns the weakness with associated attack patterns and the ATT&CK techniques those patterns map
to, connecting root cause to adversary behavior. The technique layer is resolved from this weakness's
CAPEC links, so it is only as complete as those links are: a CAPEC carrying no ATT&CK mapping
contributes none, and mitigation and detection guidance covers the techniques that do resolve —
there is none when the linked CAPECs carry no mappings.

**Include options**

- `details` — CWE object with name, description, and severity
- `capecs` — attack patterns linked to this weakness class
- `techniques` — ATT&CK techniques linked to this weakness class
- `tie` — technique likelihood predictions for resolved techniques
- `navigator` — ATT&CK Navigator layer JSON for resolved techniques
- `groups` — threat actor groups using the linked techniques
- `software` — malware and tools using the linked techniques
- `campaigns` — threat campaigns using the linked techniques
- `mitigations` — defensive courses of action per technique
- `detections` — detection data sources per technique
- `defend` — D3FEND defensive techniques and countermeasures
- `cves` — CVEs referencing this weakness (queried by weakness id, independent of the technique layer)
- `knowledgebase` — related intelligence from the knowledge base
- `summary` — AI-generated summary of the weakness and its attack implications
- `nist_controls` *(opt-in)* — NIST SP 800-53 rev 5 controls that mitigate the linked techniques,
  based on MITRE Center for Threat-Informed Defense mappings

The technique-derived layers — `groups`, `software`, `campaigns`, `mitigations`, `detections`,
`defend` and `nist_controls` — read the resolved technique set, and this endpoint resolves that
set itself from the weakness' CAPEC links, so each one answers when asked for ALONE and publishes
only its own section. `techniques[]` is the carrier that stays tied to the CAPEC walk rather than
to its own token: measured 2026-09-13 on CWE-522, `techniques`=0 with `['details','techniques']`
against `attack_patterns`=13 / `techniques`=12 with `['details','capecs','techniques']` — while a
`['nist_controls']`-only request maps that same CAPEC-linked set instead of short-circuiting to
`[]` (verified live 2026-10-15: CWE-522 alone → 198 controls, identical to the `capecs`-included
request; CWE-79 resolves no technique at all, so its `nist_controls` is empty in every shape).

Enrich an indicator of compromise with linked threat events, techniques, and predictions.

Searches our curated MISP (public threat feeds, listed at
https://crimsoncrawler.com/docs/guides/data-sources/#our-curated-misp) for the indicator (by
`value` + `type` — e.g. `ip-dst`, `domain`, `sha256`, `url`, `email-src`), extracts linked threat
actors and malware, maps to ATT&CK techniques, and generates threat predictions. Technique mappings
return even when the indicator has sparse data. An address requested as `ip-src`, `ip-dst` or
`ip` searches BOTH directions in one query — the corpus stores whichever direction the
publishing feed used — and `matched_value_types` reports what matched.

- `misp_attributes` — matching threat event attributes with event metadata
- `galaxies` — linked threat actor and malware context as compact Galaxy cluster profiles
- `galaxy_clusters_full` — cluster profiles with inbound relations (up to 30 clusters)
- `techniques` — ATT&CK techniques linked to this indicator
- `tie` — technique likelihood predictions for resolved techniques
- `warninglist` — false-positive check against known safe-list entries
- `sightings` — sighting count across linked events
- `navigator` — ATT&CK Navigator layer JSON for resolved techniques

post.description:
Enrich an open-source package — OSV.dev advisories plus full multi-source CVE enrichment.

The package-ecosystem sibling of `/v1/enrich/product`. Keyed by **ecosystem + name (+ optional
version)**, it covers the dependency-vulnerability surface (npm, PyPI, Go, Maven, crates.io,
NuGet, RubyGems, …) that the CPE-keyed product endpoint cannot reach.

OSV.dev supplies the advisories (id, cross-database aliases CVE/GHSA, fixed versions, severity,
affected ranges, references — CVE-aliased first). The CVEs those advisories alias are then
enriched through the **same multi-source enrichment chain** (CWE → CAPEC → ATT&CK techniques, EPSS,
KEV, mitigations, …) as `enrich/product`'s nested CVEs, returned under `cves[]`. Supplying a
`version` filters advisories to that version.

**Include options**

OSV-advisory verbosity:

- `details` — full advisory description and metadata
- `severity` — CVSS vectors and labels
- `affected` — affected/fixed version ranges
- `references` — advisory reference URLs

Nested CVE enrichment accepts every CVE layer listed in the request schema, including exploit
probability and exploitation evidence, weakness and ATT&CK mappings, related groups and software,
defensive guidance, source research, SSVC decisions, NIST controls, timeline and similarity context,
and AI-assisted summaries.

The default advisory set excludes restricted and unknown-licence sources. Add `osv_restricted`
to request them. Withdrawn advisories remain listed but do not count as active vulnerabilities.

Results are paged. Pass `snapshot_id` and `next_offset` from page 0 to continue; a 409 requires
a fresh walk. `advisories_discovered` and `cves_discovered` report totals, while
`cves_enrichment_limit` and `rollups_over` describe the bounded CVE enrichment.

post.description:
Find vulnerabilities affecting a product and enrich each matched CVE.

Searches by product name, version, and vendor using CPE matching, then runs every matched CVE
through the same multi-source chain as `/v1/enrich/cve`. Supply `vendor` to narrow CPE matches
and `version` to hard-filter discovered CVEs to those affecting that release. A version that
filters nothing says so: when no matched CVE states a version for the product, `errors[]` carries
`version_filter`/`version_not_applied` and the CVE set is the same for every version. NVD states
per-edition products, not one OS product — query `windows_10_22h2` (not `windows`) to filter by
Windows build number.

The include options drive the per-CVE enrichment depth (each value behaves exactly as it does on
`/v1/enrich/cve`); the product-level extras roll those results up across the matched set.

**Include options**

Per-CVE enrichment (applied to each matched CVE):

- `details` — core CVE data (CVSS, severity, description, references)
- `epss` — EPSS exploit probability score and percentile
- `kev` — Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog status
- `cwe` — root cause weakness classification
- `capec` — attack patterns for the weakness
- `techniques` — linked ATT&CK techniques
- `tie` — technique likelihood predictions
- `navigator` — ATT&CK Navigator layer JSON
- `misp` — matching threat intelligence events
- `knowledgebase` — related knowledge-base context
- `affected_products` — confirmed vulnerable software with CPE strings
- `poc` — proof-of-concept exploits from GitHub
- `groups` — threat actor groups using the linked techniques
- `software` — malware and tools using the linked techniques
- `campaigns` — threat campaigns using the linked techniques
- `mitigations` — defensive courses of action per technique
- `detections` — detection data sources per technique
- `defend` — D3FEND defensive techniques
- `exploits` — authoritative exploit objects per CVE (real evidence, not the heuristic
  `has_public_exploit` boolean)
- `ssvc` — SSVC vulnerability-prioritisation decision per CVE (CERT/CC Deployer tree,
  worst-reasonable-case defaults)
- `nist_controls` *(opt-in)* — NIST SP 800-53 rev 5 controls that mitigate the linked techniques
  (MITRE CTID mapping)
- `osv` — OSV.dev advisories and fixed versions aliased to each matched CVE

Product-level rollup:

- `summary` — AI-generated product-level brief over the matched CVE set
- `risk_summary` — aggregate risk statistics across the matched CVEs

The response also carries `likely_tactics`, an always-on set of ATT&CK tactic-class hints based on
the requested vendor. These hints are useful when matched CVEs have sparse technique coverage.
Discovery and enrichment are bounded. The response reports the discovered count, limits,
and whether discovery was truncated or its completeness is unknown.

The technique-derived per-CVE layers — `groups`, `software`, `campaigns`, `mitigations`,
`detections`, `defend` and `nist_controls` — read the technique set each nested CVE resolves for
itself, so they answer without `techniques` in the same request. The product-level `nist_controls`
rollup is the union of the nested `cves[].techniques`: the nested call is asked for those rows and
they are cleared again unless `techniques` was itself requested, so the rollup maps a real control
set without publishing a section the caller did not ask for.

post.description:
Retrieve ATT&CK technique details with threat predictions and related intelligence.

Supports a single ID (`technique_id`), batch IDs (`technique_ids`), text search (`search`), or —
ICS only — an asset class (`asset_id`, mutually exclusive with the other three), across the
`enterprise`, `ics`, or `mobile` framework (default `enterprise`). Each technique is enriched
with threat predictions (TIE) and optionally related intelligence from the knowledge base.
If all four lookup fields are omitted, the endpoint returns HTTP 200 with an empty technique list.

**`asset_id`** answers the inverse question — "which techniques target this control-system asset
class" — from the ICS corpus's own `targets` edges. The asset is returned in `asset`, and its
real targets in `techniques`; no technique is ever substituted for the asset.

**Include options**

- `details` — full technique object with tactics, mitigations, and detection guidance
- `tie` — technique likelihood predictions
- `navigator` — ATT&CK Navigator layer JSON for visualization
- `groups` — threat actor groups using the technique
- `software` — malware and tools using the technique
- `campaigns` — threat campaigns using the technique
- `mitigations` — defensive courses of action for the technique
- `detections` — detection data sources for the technique
- `defend` — D3FEND defensive techniques and countermeasures
- `cves` — CVEs mapped to the technique
- `misp` — matching threat intelligence events
- `knowledgebase` — related intelligence from the knowledge base
- `summary` — AI-generated executive brief covering the technique's usage and detection priorities
- `nist_controls` *(opt-in)* — NIST SP 800-53 rev 5 controls that mitigate the technique,
  based on MITRE Center for Threat-Informed Defense mappings
- `fraud` *(opt-in)* — `f3_techniques`: the MITRE F3 (Fight Fraud Framework) techniques whose own
  identity is this technique's ATT&CK id, on each returned technique row
- `asset_classes` *(opt-in)* — `asset_classes`: the ICS asset classes this technique targets, on
  an `ics` framework request (the corpus has no CVE→ICS technique link, so this token is
  technique-only)

post.description:
Submit a raw security event for an Event Enrichment and get back an enrichment ID to poll.

Returns an `enrichment_id` right away — the enrichment runs in the background. Poll
`GET /v1/event-enrich/{enrichment_id}` for stage-by-stage progress and the finished per-indicator
enrichment plus the aggregate event threat verdict.

The reactive counterpart to the Artifact + Inventory Enrichers: hand it a raw event (a Defender
XDR / Sentinel alert, a SIEM/EDR log line, any JSON or text) and CC extracts the indicators
(CVEs / ATT&CK techniques / IOCs / products) the same deterministic way the Artifact Enricher
does, enriches each against the authoritative CTI sources, and aggregates a per-event verdict —
so a SOC platform submits one alert here instead of looping the single `/v1/enrich/*` endpoints.

An ACCEPTED submission (202) consumes one request unit; a refused one (429/503) and every poll consume
none. Each API key can run 3 Artifact,
Inventory, or Event Enrichments at once and can hold 20 running or queued jobs across all three
engines. Jobs beyond the running limit remain `queued`; a full queue returns 429, and that cap is
enforced atomically, so simultaneous submits cannot push an owner past it. If queue state cannot
be verified, the request returns 503 and no job is created.

`/v1/inventory-enrich/{enrichment_id}` for stage progress and the finished findings.

jointly). Jobs

post.description:
Search across multiple threat intelligence knowledge bases simultaneously.

Searches the knowledge bases selected in `sources`, including ATT&CK, CWE, CAPEC, ATLAS,
DISARM, F3, CLOAK, location, and sector records. Each result has a canonical `_source` label.
Use `types` to restrict compatible object types within the selected sources.

**Sources**

- `attack` — ATT&CK Enterprise objects
- `attack-enterprise` — ATT&CK Enterprise objects
- `attack-ics` — ATT&CK ICS objects
- `attack-mobile` — ATT&CK Mobile objects
- `cwe` — CWE weaknesses
- `capec` — CAPEC attack patterns
- `atlas` — MITRE ATLAS adversarial ML techniques
- `disarm` — DISARM influence-operation techniques
- `f3` — MITRE Fight Fraud Framework (F3) financial-crime techniques
- `cloak` — CLOAK concealment layers for online anonymity
- `location` — geographic threat-landscape entries
- `sector` — industry-sector threat profiles

An ATT&CK matrix source is not techniques-only: the same `attack` search also returns Analytics
(`AN####`, e.g. "Analytic 0292") and tactic rows, and neither belongs to a `types` value the
filter accepts, so they cannot be excluded. Filter on the row's own id prefix (or on
`_source` + the presence of `technique_id`) if you need techniques alone.

**Type filters**

- `attack-pattern` — ATT&CK techniques and CAPEC patterns
- `intrusion-set` — threat actor groups
- `malware` — malware families
- `tool` — adversary tooling
- `campaign` — threat campaigns
- `weakness` — CWE weaknesses
- `course-of-action` — mitigations and countermeasures

Each result is tagged with its knowledge base in `_source`. Results arrive in the knowledge base's
own ranking order; no relevance score is attached. The former `relevance_score` was a function
of the row's position **on its page** — 1.0 for the first row of every page, 0.5 for the last, so
page 2's worst row could outrank page 1's best and tightening `limit` inflated the top rows
(measured 2026-09-13: T1558.002 read 0.60 / 0.80 / 0.90 at `limit` 5 / 10 / 20, and the first row
of pages 1, 2 and 3 all read 1.0). Removed rather than left as a rank dressed up as a similarity.
The `errors` array reports any partial failures.

200.description: Search completed. The response contains matching records and any available metadata; `errors[]` lists partial source failures.

post.description:
Search vulnerabilities by ID, weakness, product, severity, exploit status, technique, and date range.

Combine any of the filters below to scope the result set. Each result carries severity, a public-exploit
count, an EPSS probability with its percentile rank, and a weaponization score. Provide at least one
search parameter.

**Filters**

- `cve_id` — direct CVE lookup (e.g. `CVE-2026-26929`)
- `query` — compatibility field; free-text matching is not currently supported and this value
  does not filter results
- `cwe_id` — filter by weakness type (e.g. `CWE-79`)
- `cpe` — filter by affected product (CPE string)
- `attack_id` — filter CVEs linked to an ATT&CK technique (e.g. `T1078`). Links come from the
  CVE→CWE→CAPEC→ATT&CK chain, which MITRE's CAPEC taxonomy maps only in part, so several common
  techniques (`T1190`, `T1059`, `T1068`) have no link there and always return nothing
- `capec_id` — filter CVEs linked to a CAPEC attack pattern (e.g. `CAPEC-665`)
- `cvss_min` — minimum CVSS v3.1 base score (`0.0`-`10.0`)
- `cvss_v2_min` — minimum CVSS v2 base score (`0.0`-`10.0`)
- `cvss_v4_min` — minimum CVSS v4 base score (`0.0`-`10.0`)
- `epss_min` — minimum EPSS score (`0.0`-`1.0`)
- `epss_percentile_min` — minimum EPSS percentile (`0.0`-`1.0`), rank against all CVEs rather than the raw score
- `kev_only` — only return CVEs in the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
- `cpes_not_vulnerable` — only CVEs whose `not_vulnerable` set carries this CPE 2.3 string (a
  positive containment filter, not an exclusion — a CPE no CVE lists there returns nothing)
- `created_by_ref` — filter by CNA or numbering-authority identity STIX ID
- `stix_id` — filter by exact vulnerability STIX ID
- `modified_min` / `modified_max` — restrict to a modification-date range
- `created_min` / `created_max` — restrict to a creation-date range
- `vuln_status` — vulnerability status: `Received`, `Awaiting Analysis`, `Undergoing Analysis`,
  `Analyzed`, `Modified`, `Deferred`, `Rejected`

**Sort options**

- `created_ascending` — oldest creation date first
- `created_descending` — newest creation date first
- `modified_ascending` — oldest modification date first
- `modified_descending` — newest modification date first
- `epss_score_descending` — highest EPSS score first
- `x_opencti_cvss_base_score_descending` — highest CVSS base score first

**Include options**

- `details` — full vulnerability detail per result
- `statistics` — corpus coverage and freshness (counts, deltas, CVSS/EPSS distributions)
- `cna` — the CNA directory for the search
- `epss_reports` — EPSS scores for exactly the CVEs this search returned (`epss_reports`,
  with the source's own `epss_reports_total` / `epss_reports_page` metadata)
- `kb_rankings` — up to 100 CVE-volume ranking rows per knowledge base, without yearly trends
- `kb_rankings_full` — all fetched ranking rows and yearly trends

All except `kb_rankings_full` are default. An explicit include replaces the default;
omitted layers return empty arrays. The `errors` array reports any partial failures.

200.description: Search completed. The response contains matching records and any available metadata; `errors[]` lists partial source failures.

post.description:
Search the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

Look up a specific CVE by ID, or browse KEV entries. Each result carries an EPSS score, a public-exploit
count, and a weaponization score.

**Filters**

- `cve_id` — check one CVE against the KEV catalog
- `ransomware_status` — `Known` (confirmed ransomware campaign use) or `Unknown` (unconfirmed)

**Include options**

- `statistics` — deployment-wide corpus coverage (CVE/KEV totals, per-year counts, and the
  d1/d7/d30/d365 creation deltas), the same block `/v1/search/cve` returns. The KEV half
  (`kev_by_year`, `kev_created_since`) is the part this surface answers for directly.

Each result is the catalog entry as this endpoint's sources publish it. `vendor_project` and
`product` ride the catalog mirror's own KEV report — `external_references` rows the Vulmatch KEV
ingest now publishes from CISA's `vendorProject`/`product` columns — so they populate here once
that deployment has run the one-time KEV backfill and read null before it (`POST
/api/v1/arango-cve-processor/cve-kev/`; see `.claude/rules/vulmatch.md`, "KEV backfill").
`forensic_triage` (plus the `supplemented_from` mark) is the one that comes from CISA's own KEV
record alone and is therefore always null here: CVE enrichment's `cisa_kev` reads it
(`/v1/enrich/cve`, plus product, package and batch paths that delegate to it).

Omitted filters are ignored. The `errors` array reports any partial failures.
