post.description:
Search our curated MISP by indicator, event text, or event ID.

Returns matching threat events and indicators with actor and malware context. Our curated MISP pulls
a small set of public feeds on a daily schedule; the full list is at https://crimsoncrawler.com/docs/guides/data-sources/#our-curated-misp.

**Filters**

- `value` — indicator value to match (IP, hash, domain, etc.)
- `eventinfo` — search events by title or description text
- `event_id` — look up one event directly by ID
- `type_attribute` — restrict to one attribute type (e.g. `ip-dst`, `md5`, `domain`)
- `category` — restrict to one MISP attribute category (e.g. `Network activity`, `Payload delivery`)
- `tags` — match any of the given tags (supports `tlp:` prefixes and galaxy cluster names)
- `to_ids` — attribute selector: `true` returns only attributes flagged for IDS detection
  (high-confidence indicators), `false` only attributes NOT flagged. Omitting it does not filter.
- `threat_level_id` — event threat level: `1` (high), `2` (medium), `3` (low), `4` (undefined)
- `date_from` / `date_to` — restrict to an event date range (`YYYY-MM-DD`)
- `published` — restrict to events published by their owning org (excludes analyst drafts)

Attribute filters (`value`, `type_attribute`, `category`, `tags`, `to_ids`) search attributes
only; event filters (`eventinfo`, `published`) search events only; `event_id` looks one event up
directly. `threat_level_id` and the date range apply to BOTH kinds, so a request carrying only
those — with no attribute, event, or event-ID selector — searches attributes and events.
Explicitly scoped requests keep their scope; a common filter never broadens one.

A request with no content selector and no filter reads no content: `attributes`, `events`, and
`feed_previews` all come back empty, with a 200 rather than an error. Scheduling nothing there
is deliberate, because an unfiltered sweep of the whole instance is not what this endpoint
answers. The instance-level include layers still respond, since they don't depend on a match:
`version` reports the MISP build and `tags` returns one page of tag names.

**Include options**

- `sightings` — adds the event-level sighting records (deduplicated across each event's own
  attributes and `/sightings/index`). Per-attribute `sighting_count` / `sightings` on the
  returned attribute rows come from the correlation join that always runs, so they are present
  with or without this token; the token governs the event-level reads.
- `event_reports` — the analyst-written reports attached to the returned events
- `stats` — each returned event's composition (attributes by category, objects by name)
- `version` — the MISP build behind the data (`misp_version`)
- `tags` — one page of the instance's tag names (`tag_names` + `tag_names_total`)
- `feeds` — read-only previews of the feeds that carried the returned indicators
- `objects` — resolve composite-object reference targets the search payload left unresolved
- `misp_events_full` — full event bodies; otherwise event rows are summarized

`event_reports`, `tags`, and `version` are on by default. An explicit include replaces them.
Event searches request ascending event IDs. Pages are not a snapshot; edits or deletions may shift
results between requests, and cached pages may reflect an earlier MISP state.

Omitted filters are ignored. The `errors` array reports any partial failures.

200.description: Search completed. The response contains matching records and any available metadata; `errors[]` lists partial source failures.

post.description:
List products from a vendor, or enumerate the vendor directory.

Pass `vendor` for up to `limit` known products from the CPE dictionary — pass a returned CPE
string to `/v1/search/cve` as the `cpe` filter to find vulnerabilities for that product. A
multi-version product contributes one row per CPE entry, and `total_products` counts the
distinct products those rows represent. Omit `vendor` (optionally with `q`) to enumerate the
CPE vendor directory with product counts.

The `errors` array reports any partial failures.

200.description: Search completed. The response contains matching records and any available metadata; `errors[]` lists partial source failures.

tags.description: Resolve one CVE, product, open-source package, weakness, ATT&CK object, indicator, location, sector, D3FEND object, or public PoC source into linked threat and defense intelligence. Each operation documents its accepted `include` values; a supplied list replaces that operation's defaults. Omitted layers stay null or empty. Source gaps are reported in `errors[]` without discarding successful data. Use `/v1/enrich/batch` for up to 50 mixed entities in one request.
tags.name: enrichment

tags.description: Find source records before enriching them: CVEs, ATT&CK/CWE/CAPEC objects, CISA KEV entries, MISP events and attributes, knowledge-base passages, vendors, D3FEND objects, and public proof-of-concept repositories. Filters, pagination, and sort options differ by source and are defined on each request schema. Results preserve partial source failures in `errors[]`.
tags.name: search

tags.description: Evaluate a collection rather than one entity. Measure ATT&CK technique coverage, rank CVE exposure, map threat-group overlap, or summarize an IOC portfolio. `include` selects optional analysis layers and replaces the endpoint's defaults. Responses keep resolved findings when a source fails and identify the gap in `errors[]`.
tags.name: assess

tags.description: Submit pasted security text or supported files for asynchronous Artifact Enrichment, then poll the returned `enrichment_id`. The engine extracts security references and returns per-reference evidence, SSVC-derived actions, prioritization, citations, defensive guidance, attack paths, corroboration, and requested exports. The `include` list selects report sections, not analysis depth. Three jobs run per API key; up to 20 may be running or queued. Polls consume no plan units.
tags.name: artifact-enrich

tags.description: Submit up to 200 software, package, operating-system, or device assets for asynchronous Inventory Enrichment, then poll the returned `enrichment_id`. Results contain per-asset CVE findings, remediation guidance, portfolio rollups, and optional attachment enrichment. The request's `include` list controls per-CVE depth. Three jobs run per API key; up to 20 may be running or queued. Polls consume no plan units.
tags.name: inventory-enrich

tags.description: Submit one raw security event (a Defender XDR / Sentinel alert, a SIEM/EDR log line, any JSON or text) for asynchronous Event Enrichment, then poll the returned `enrichment_id`. The engine extracts the indicators server-side, enriches them through the same authoritative CTI sources as the single-entity endpoints, and returns per-indicator verdicts plus an aggregate event threat assessment. Three jobs run per API key; up to 20 may be running or queued. Polls consume no plan units.
tags.name: event-enrich
